sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Platform engineer with **twelve years** across payments, streaming data and developer tooling, most of it spent making other teams faster rather than shipping features directly. Owns the migration strategy for a 400-service estate, the internal deployment platform three hundred engineers use daily, and the incident practice behind a 99.99% availability target. Comfortable operating between architecture review and a 3am page.

bullets: Led the migration of 400 services from a shared Kubernetes cluster to per-team clusters with a golden-path Terraform module, cutting median deploy time from 22 minutes to 4 and removing the noisy-neighbour class of incident entirely.
Designed the multi-region active-active topology for the card authorisation path, holding 99.99% availability through two full regional failovers.
Built the internal developer portal that now fronts every service catalogue, runbook and on-call rota, adopted by 38 of 41 teams within two quarters.
Chaired the architecture review board and rewrote the RFC process, reducing mean time from proposal to decision from 6 weeks to 9 days.
Cut cloud spend 31% through commitment planning, right-sizing and killing 74 orphaned environments.
Replaced a nightly Spark batch with a Flink pipeline processing 2.4M events per second, dropping end-to-end data lag from 11 hours to under 90 seconds.
Introduced schema registry and contract tests across 60 producers, ending the recurring class of silent downstream breakage.
Owned the cost model for the data lake, cutting storage spend 44% with tiering and compaction without changing a single query.
Mentored six engineers to senior, three of whom now lead their own platform teams.
Built the FHIR-compliant integration layer connecting 19 hospital systems, passing NHS Digital assurance first time.
Introduced event sourcing for the patient record service, which made a two-year audit backlog answerable in minutes.
Took the service from 92% to 99.95% availability by fixing connection pooling, adding load shedding and rewriting the retry policy.
Wrote the route optimisation service in Go, cutting average planned distance per vehicle 12%.
Migrated the monolith's billing module to its own service with zero downtime and no customer-visible change.
Built the reporting API backing the customer dashboard, still in production a decade later.
Added the first CI pipeline the company had, taking release from a manual afternoon to eleven minutes.

items.name: driftwatch
bullets: Open-source Terraform drift detector, 3.2k stars, used in production by four companies I know of and probably more I do not.

items.name: slowquery
bullets: Postgres query plan differ that flags regressions between releases; wrote it after a 3am page and never had that page again.

items.note: First-class honours. Thesis on consensus under partial synchrony.
